title: Feijão Dam I / Brumadinho: upstream tailings dam, flow liquefaction, monitoring non-legibility, and high-consequence exposure
summary: Brumadinho is encoded as a high-sensitivity tailings failure where upstream construction, drainage/water/saturation, creep/strength loss, sudden brittle response, monitoring non-legibility, and consequence exposure are all essential to the record.

status_history.note: Added as rev0026 impoundment/tailings failure lane record.

place.location: Córrego do Feijão Mine near Brumadinho, Minas Gerais, Brazil

claims.claim: ASDSO’s case study says Dam B-1 was constructed using the upstream construction method from 1976 to 2013 in 10 raises, and reached a maximum height of 86 m with a crest length of 720 m.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: ASDSO’s case study says Dam B-1 failed at 12:28 pm on January 25, 2019, killing 272 people and releasing 9.7 million m3 of liquefied mining waste downstream.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The expert panel report states that its mandate was to assess technical causes and did not assess corporate or personal responsibility for the failure.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The expert panel concluded that sudden strength loss and resulting failure of a marginally stable dam was due to a critical combination of ongoing internal strains from creep and strength reduction from loss of suction in the unsaturated zone caused by cumulative rainfall, including intense rainfall toward the end of 2018.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The expert panel also said the design/construction produced a steep dam with insufficient drainage and high water levels; monitoring devices did not detect precursors, and the failure was sudden and abrupt because of high shear stresses and brittle undrained tailings response.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: ASDSO’s case study records later interpretive caution: another expert panel and a 2024 study proposed different trigger/emphasis accounts, so this cube must not freeze Brumadinho as a single settled causal story beyond the cited surfaces.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

sequence_of_events: Rapid failure at Dam B-1; liquefied tailings released downstream; technical report reconstructed deformation, seepage, stability, rainfall, creep, and monitoring data.
type_payload.proximate_cause: flow/static liquefaction and brittle undrained strength loss in marginally stable tailings
contributing_factors: lack of sufficient drainage / high water level
loss of suction from cumulative/intense rainfall
monitoring did not make precursor state actionable
alarm/emergency warning limits under rapid progression
latent_conditions: high-consequence exposure near mine facilities and downstream communities
monitoring is not equivalent to actionable state legibility
commissioned technical-cause report scope excludes responsibility

handling_notes: Preserve casualty and community dignity; avoid spectacle and avoid using disasters as clever engineering anecdotes.
Separate physical mechanism, design/construction/operation history, monitoring or warning limits, regulatory/governance context, and post-event correction rails.
This record is historical/evidentiary infrastructure, not current engineering, mining, dam-safety, legal, or emergency-management advice.

unknowns: Legal/responsibility determinations are outside this record’s technical-cause scope.
The causal trigger literature contains competing emphases; this record is deliberately source-scoped and not final.
next_actions: Add legal/governance child records only from appropriate official proceedings.
